name: Ostara
date_note: Around March 20 (the spring equinox). Easter is a separate Christian festival that often falls nearby.
history: Ostara is a modern Wiccan name for the spring equinox, and its link to a goddess named Eostre is a popular claim that historians consider weakly supported. Eggs are the most common symbolic food in modern Ostara menus. Hot cross buns are a medieval English Easter food, and their earliest history is debated.
confidence: Eggs and spring greens are seasonal. The Eostre link and the origin of hot cross buns are uncertain.

sources.title: Pagan Grimoire: Ostara recipes and traditional foods

dishes.name: Spiced hot cross buns
dishes.ritual_note: Hot cross buns are a shared Easter food. Eat them with others for good luck, the way many people do.
ingredients: For the crosses: 50 g plain flour and about 3 tbsp water
2 tbsp apricot jam, warmed, for glazing
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, spices and lemon zest. Add the egg, milk and melted butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour, until doubled. Knead the currants in gently.
Divide into 12 balls and place them close together in a greased tin. Cover and prove for 45 minutes.
Mix the plain flour with water to a thick paste. Pipe a cross over each bun.
Bake at 200 C (180 C fan) for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden. Brush with warm jam while hot.
dishes.safety: Keep the cross paste thick so it does not run off the buns.

dishes.name: Spring herb frittata
dishes.ritual_note: Eggs are the most common symbolic food of Ostara. Use whatever spring greens you can find.
ingredients: 100 g asparagus, woody ends snapped off and cut into short lengths
steps: Heat the grill to medium. Beat the eggs with salt, pepper and most of the herbs.
Warm the oil in an ovenproof frying pan. Cook the asparagus and spring onions for 3 minutes, then add the spinach and wilt it.
Pour in the eggs, sprinkle with cheese, and cook gently on the hob for 4 to 5 minutes, until the base is set.
Finish under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until the top is set and golden. Scatter with the remaining herbs and slice.
dishes.safety: Use a pan with an ovenproof handle, and take care when handling the hot pan.
